title: The car that teleported backward
blurb: Last-write-wins updates and dropped geofence checks.
prompt: The dispatch map showed a truck six blocks behind its actual position, because a delayed cellular update wrote last, and a warehouse geofence alert never fired when the check call timed out. Review it, fix it, and prove positions compare by timestamp and alerts cannot be lost or doubled.
aiNote: The draft writes the latest-arriving position regardless of its timestamp, so delayed packets roll a vehicle's state backward, and it drops geofence checks on timeout, then retries them under fresh keys so a generated alert can duplicate.
testIdea: Deliver a new position then a delayed older one and assert the newer state stands; time out a geofence check and assert it retries under the same sequence key; check the snapshot freshness bound across lazily refreshed vehicles.
followUps: What clock assumptions does a device sequence survive?
How fresh must a dispatch snapshot be to be usable?
Which alerts may never be dropped even under load?
